scope: Rust output for v5 prompts: a parent and a child resource joined by a foreign key, a restricted parent delete answering 409, child routes scoped to their parent, timestamps, the atomic with-children batch of 1 to 20 children, the migration and the product tests.

target_contract.note: Unchanged by #49. As amendment 1 requires, the v5 tables default their timestamps to now().

gate.rule: bundle_checks, assemble_refusals and product_gates pass for every v1 to v5 acceptance case, and every case passes parity with the Rust files the gates built

assemble_refusal_notes: A6 now uses its frozen base, the example-v5 Rust bundle. In #48 it used the example-v1 bundle because v5 answered NOT_IMPLEMENTED.

python.rule: every frozen acceptance case passes on its Python product

faults.rule: every seeded fault fails the suite in its category, and every category has one

parity.rule: every v1 to v5 case: Python and Rust transcripts equal, no oracle failure on either side, and the Rust side of D1 to D5 as frozen

target_checks.python_unchanged: Every source form without target, and with target python, equals the read-only reference compiler on 8765 byte for byte, and its bundle assembles to the same Python file bytes on both.

byte_identity: Before and after the change, the QA compiler gave the same files for all 115 Python products and for the 112 v1 to v4 Rust products; only the 3 v5 Rust products are new.

code_review.reviewer: an independent read-only review agent, separate from the author session
code_review.scope: som-targets/src/rust/render/related.rs, render.rs, mod.rs, rust-catalog.v1.json, check_rust_products.py, check_targets.py, behavior/check_behavior.py and README
code_review.verdict: no high findings; the medium finding is fixed; two low findings are accepted as recorded limitations

fixed.finding: batch_is_atomic used sample rows 6 to 8, so a unique NOT NULL bool on the parent or the child gave a false 409 on the final batch
fixed.fix: the test uses rows 1 and 2 and copies children[0] into children[1]; rows 0, 1 and 2 never collide on a unique value
fixed.check: a custom v5 product with unique required bools on the parent and the child passed all eight product gates

accepted.finding: a PATCH that changes no value still moves updated_at
accepted.reason: same as the v1 to v4 Rust products; timestamp values are normalized by the behavior suite

accepted.finding: a rejected batch child loc has no child index

confirmed: no SQL built from request text
v1 to v4 Rust output unchanged

environment.qa: som-targets debug build on 127.0.0.1:18901; default on 127.0.0.1:8765 unchanged, read-only compile and assemble calls only
environment.postgres: a fresh cluster of the pinned PostgreSQL 17.7 binaries (sha256 checked) per run on a port in 18919-18999, one fresh database per product; stopped at the end of the run
environment.toolchain: rustc and cargo 1.96.1 and rustfmt 1.9.0 per contracts/rust-output-v1/toolchain.json; reference Cargo.lock, offline
environment.python_qa_tools: a scratch virtual environment with fastapi 0.118.0, uvicorn 0.53.0, sqlalchemy 2.0.44, psycopg[binary] 3.3.6, alembic 1.20.0, pydantic 2.11.9 from PyPI; QA only

limitations: Raw exchanges are kept on this host only and are not published; this file keeps their sha256. Rust products were built and run on this host only. No binaries or raw measurements are published. A PATCH that changes no value still moves updated_at, as in the v1 to v4 Rust products; the behavior suite normalizes timestamp values, so it does not compare this. A rejected batch child reports a loc without the child index; parity compares loc[0] only.
